skill.name: bv
skill.description: Beads Viewer helps agents and developers triage Beads projects with graph metrics, robot-mode summaries, and execution plans.
skill.summary: Triage Beads work with graph metrics, blocker analysis, and non-interactive robot commands.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

security_audit.summary: All 66 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced command examples, or graph terminology in SKILL.md. The skill documents local CLI use for Beads triage and does not contain executable code, network calls, secret access, prompt injection, or host reconnaissance instructions.

static_findings.snippet: A graph-aware triage engine for Beads projects (`.beads/beads.jsonl`). Computes 9 graph metrics, gen
**Never run bare `bv`**. It launches an interactive TUI that blocks your session.
Always check `status` field in output. For large graphs (>500 nodes), some metrics may be `approx` o
| `default` | All open issues sorted by priority |
| `quick-wins` | Easy P2/P3 items with no blockers |
BV reads from `.beads/beads.jsonl` created by the `bd` CLI:
| TUI blocks agent | Use `--robot-*` flags only |
| Stale metrics | Check `status` field, results cached by `data_hash` |
| Wrong recommendations | Use `--recipe actionable` to filter to ready work |
| **Topo Sort** | Valid execution order | Work queue foundation |

content.user_title: Prioritize Beads Work with Graph Metrics
content.value_statement: Teams often miss blockers and cycles when reading issue lists by hand. This skill turns Beads data into focused triage, planning, and agent workflow guidance.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes Beads project status using robot triage output.
Identifies blockers, bottlenecks, quick wins, and top task recommendations.
Uses graph metrics such as PageRank, betweenness, critical path, and cycles.
Plans parallel work tracks from dependency relationships.
Checks metric status, data hashes, and historical diff context.
Guides agents to use non-interactive robot flags instead of TUI mode.
limitations: Requires the bv and bd CLIs to be installed in the active project.
Works on Beads data stored in .beads/beads.jsonl.
Large graphs may return approximate, skipped, or timed out metrics.
Recommendations depend on current bead data quality and dependency links.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Release Blockers
use_cases.description: Find high-impact tasks, dependency bottlenecks, and cycle risks before assigning release work.

use_cases.title: Select the Next Agent Task
use_cases.description: Use robot-mode triage to choose one actionable task and explain why it should be claimed.

use_cases.title: Review Project Dependency Health
use_cases.description: Inspect label health, graph density, stale work, and structural issues across a Beads project.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Next Beads Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Beads Viewer robot mode to identify the best next task. Explain the task, why it matters, and any blockers to check.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Parallel Work Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the current Beads project and create parallel execution tracks. Highlight the highest-impact blocker in each track.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Graph Health
prompt_templates.prompt: Review graph metrics for cycles, bottlenecks, keystones, and label health. Summarize risks that should be fixed before new work starts.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Historical Project Drift
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current Beads triage with a historical reference. Explain changed blockers, new dependency risks, and priority shifts.

output_examples.input: Find the next task in this Beads project.
output_examples.output: The top recommendation is ready to claim and has strong unblock value. It should be handled before lower-impact quick wins.

output_examples.input: Review graph health before planning a sprint.
output_examples.output: The project has several blocked items and one cycle risk. Clear the cycle first, then assign independent tracks by label.

output_examples.input: Explain why the suggested task is important.
output_examples.output: The task sits on a dependency path used by multiple open items. Completing it should reduce downstream waiting time.

best_practices: Start with robot triage before opening detailed metric views.
Check cycle results before claiming work.
Verify data hash and metric status when comparing outputs.
anti_patterns: Running the interactive TUI in an agent session.
Prioritizing by title or priority only without graph context.
Ignoring approximate or skipped metric status on large projects.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes Beads project data and explains graph-aware triage results from Beads Viewer.

faq.question: Does it replace the bd CLI?
faq.answer: No. It guides use of bv and bd commands, but those tools still perform the project operations.

faq.question: Why should agents avoid bare bv?
faq.answer: Bare bv opens an interactive TUI, which can block an automated agent session.

faq.question: Can it find circular dependencies?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill directs users to robot insights that report cycle information for the Beads graph.

faq.question: Can it plan work for multiple people?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize parallel work tracks and identify blockers that affect each track.

faq.question: What data must already exist?
faq.answer: The project needs Beads data in .beads/beads.jsonl and the related CLI tools available locally.
